standard_prerequisites.name: Half adjoint equivalence and right inverses
standard_prerequisites.statement: A half adjoint equivalence on f consists of an inverse with a homotopy, and over each right inverse of f there is a type of coherence data relating the two triangle identities.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the hypothesis and the type shown contractible.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherence as a path in a fiber
standard_prerequisites.statement: The coherence type is equivalent to a dependent product over the domain of path types inside the fibers of f.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the goal to a pointwise statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of the fiber and of its path spaces
standard_prerequisites.statement: In a half adjoint equivalence the fiber of f over a point is contractible, and a path space of a contractible type is contractible.

core_obligations: Use the identification of the coherence type with the dependent product of path types inside the fibers, together with the fact that dependent function types preserve contractibility, to reduce the goal to a pointwise claim (source lines 355-355).
For each point of the domain, exhibit the required path type inside the fiber of f and note that the fiber is contractible by the half adjoint structure (source lines 356-356).
Conclude contractibility of that path space since path spaces of contractible types are contractible (source lines 356-357).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the coherence type to a dependent product of path types in fibers.
Contractibility of the fiber and of its path space closes the argument.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 351-353 (book Lemma 4.2.12): if f is a half adjoint equivalence then for every right inverse with its homotopy the coherence type over that pair is contractible. The statement is a contractibility claim about data attached to a pair, and the proof (source lines 354-357) has to first replace the coherence type by a dependent product of path types inside the fibers, which is what makes it possible to argue pointwise, and then to notice that the fiber of a half adjoint equivalence is contractible so that each required path space is contractible as well. The reduction of the coherence datum to a pointwise path statement is the content and the statement shows none of it.
